description: §17.1.2 — `if=` on an `<each>` gates THE WHOLE ITERATED LIST, `<empty>` INCLUDED. `@shown` seeds false and nothing flips it, so li.row must be count 0. #clear then empties the collection, which is the discriminating step: the `<empty>` fallback is the branch an implementation that gated only the ROW render would still emit, so #none must ALSO be count 0. Before this widening `if=` generated ZERO code here and the list rendered unconditionally. `<each>` is the one host with no element to wrap — its mount is a COMMENT FENCE, because an element wrapper is invalid directly inside `<ul>`/`<tbody>`/`<select>` — so the whole `#list` must contain no `li` of either kind.
rationale: §17.1.2's table admits `if=` on `<each>` (§17.7) and scopes §17.1 semantics to "the whole iterated list, INCLUDING `<empty>`". §17.1.2.1 adds: "For `<each if=expr>`: the iterated collection is not read and no rows are reconciled while `expr` is false; the keyed reconciler state is rebuilt on re-entry." §17.1 governs the absence itself — "It does not exist in the DOM" — and §17.2's "`show=` hides, `if=` removes" rules out a visibility lowering.
